five_second.sells: online drawing/art courses framed as a mindfulness and manifestation practice (Neurographica, chakras, spirals, Zentangle-style drawing)
five_second.for_whom: self-development-minded creatives, wellness people looking to add a drawing practice

features_used.moment: Opened the menu right away to find About Me before looking at any course, which is just how I shop.
Found a full bio for a real named founder, Anna Denning, with a co-author credit (Colette Baron-Reid) and a book published by Hay House, not just vague hype.
Tapped the Instagram icon to see if the account was live like I always do, and it threw me onto a broken instagram.com error page instead of showing the account.
Scanned the course list to see how many different offerings there were before picking one to dig into.
This course named a completely different, specific teacher (Ann Diane Tai, Certified Zentangle Teacher CZT #11) with a detailed, oddly specific bio about her mother and co-authored books.
Confirmed this course was Anna Denning's own, matching her About page identity, which felt consistent, though the copy here leaned more into vague wellness hype without a price shown.
This was the big one: 28 real named facilitators, each with their own Instagram, Facebook, personal website, or email listed individually.
Tapped through to one facilitator's own site (artfromhearts.co.uk) and it was a real, live, matching personal art site, not a dead link.

features_looked_for_but_missing: a photo or short video of Anna Denning actually drawing or teaching, to put a face to the bio
visible pricing on the course pages themselves without clicking Buy/Join
student reviews attached to real names on the individual course pages
feature_that_most_helped_the_decision: the Certified Facilitators Directory listing 28 real named people with live personal websites and social links
feature_that_most_hurt_the_decision: the Instagram icon leading to a broken off-site error page instead of letting me verify the main account

friction.moment: Landing page already had two separate email capture forms visible before I'd learned anything about who teaches here.
Tapping the Instagram social icon sent me off-site to an error page (HTTP 429), so I couldn't confirm the account was active myself.
The Instagram handle shown in the top nav (@neurographics.art) didn't match the one in the footer (@annadenningart), which made me unsure which was the real account.
The 7 Chakras course page used breathy wellness language (Energy Boost, Deep Dive) with no visible price, feeling closer to funnel copy than the Zendala page did.

delight.moment: The Zendala course teacher bio got specific fast: certification number, her mother's certification number, and the fact they'd co-authored books together in Mandarin Chinese.
Finding a whole directory of 28 named, individually-linked facilitators was more transparency than I expected from a site like this.

what_earned_it: a real named founder with a traditionally published book (Hay House) and a named co-author
individual course pages crediting specific, differently-named teachers with verifiable-sounding credentials
a large directory of named facilitators with working personal websites and social links, one of which I verified myself
trust.what_it_would_take: seeing an actual photo or video of Anna Denning herself drawing or teaching on the site, and having the main Instagram link actually load so I could check it directly

brand_recall.tell_a_friend_one_sentence: It's a spiritual-drawing course site (chakras, manifesting, Zentangle) run by an author named Anna Denning, but unlike most of these, each course actually names its real teacher and there's a whole directory of dozens of named, checkable facilitators.
brand_recall.product_remembered: the Zendala Drawing Course, taught by Ann Tai
